rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, Tables 4-6, Figs 2-6 - the authors collected their own canopy reflectance spectra (FieldSpec 3) from 172 cotton plants in three fields in Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu during 2010-11, with chlorophyll and relative water content measurements, and derived and regressed new leafhopper indices (LHI 1-4) against infestation grades.
rows.notes: The study is a primary field study on detection: it shows that hyperspectral reflectance and the proposed LHI 2 and LHI 4 indices correlate with visually graded leafhopper severity on individual cotton plants (R2 0.461-0.850 across three fields). It does not test or report any use of these indices to guide farmer action or to prevent further pest damage; the pest_control function in the passage is only a downstream consequence the study does not evaluate. Measurements are per-plant with a ground-based radiometer, not area mapping. The study itself notes weaker and inconsistent relationships in Field 1 and attributes this to unmeasured soil, weather, cultivar and population factors, and chlorophyll/RWC could not be sampled in Field 3 - these would be limitations relevant to detection, not to the claimed control effect.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is cited for the Leafhopper Index (LHI); its own result is detection of leafhopper severity, a precondition of the pest-control effect claimed in the passage.
